regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Neoadjuvant or adjuvant · early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Two chemotherapy phases can reduce the risk of recurrence. Before surgery, treatment can also shrink the cancer. Your MDT confirms the indication and whether any separate targeted or endocrine treatment is needed.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Neoadjuvant or adjuvant · early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Doxorubicin interferes with enzymes and DNA processes needed for cell division. It can also affect heart muscle, so the team considers previous exposure and cardiac risk. Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body and damages DNA. This helps stop dividing cancer cells but can also affect blood-cell production and reproductive tissues. Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Four AC treatments 14 days apart, followed 14 days after the last AC by 12 weekly paclitaxel doses, subject to recovery and review.
key_points: No trastuzumab phase is automatically part of NCCP 00485. HER2-directed treatment needs its own indication and cardiac plan.
NCCP cardiac wording differs at exactly LVEF 50%; the decision tool flags this for review.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: For eligible higher-risk HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer, ribociclib is added to endocrine therapy to reduce recurrence risk.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant · HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Ribociclib blocks CDK4 and CDK6, proteins that help cells move through the cycle of division. Endocrine therapy reduces the hormone signal that can drive HR-positive breast cancer. An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production. Premenopausal patients need an agreed ovarian-suppression plan; men also require the appropriate hormonal partner plan. The endocrine schedule continues separately from the ribociclib breaks.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.
key_points: Days 1–21: ribociclib. Days 22–28: break. The endocrine partner follows its own schedule. Day 25–26 is a local operational option, not an NCCP replacement for early checks.
Adjuvant starting dose is 400 mg; the lower level is 200 mg. Do not import the metastatic 600 mg starting schedule.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Advanced / metastatic · previously treated HER2-positive breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: The three medicines work together to control previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. Treatment is reviewed regularly for benefit, symptoms and side effects.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced / metastatic · previously treated HER2-positive breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Tucatinib reduces signalling from the internal part of HER2. It works alongside trastuzumab and capecitabine, which act in different ways. Its tablet schedule continues through the capecitabine break. The body converts capecitabine into fluorouracil, which disrupts DNA and RNA processes needed for cell growth. Tablets are active chemotherapy; taking them at home still requires a clear monitoring and interruption plan. Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Tucatinib twice daily every day; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14 then off on Days 15–21; IV trastuzumab every 21 days. Continue while beneficial and tolerated, with clinician-approved changes.
key_points: Tumour markers, if useful, supplement symptoms and imaging. They must not alone decide whether treatment is working or should change.
Brain metastases were included in HER2CLIMB, but this does not set a universal brain MRI interval. Confirm the individual CNS imaging / radiotherapy plan.
Tucatinib can raise creatinine through transporter effects. Assess true renal function and dehydration before adjusting capecitabine; do not dismiss a rise automatically.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: HER2-positive early breast cancer · before surgery
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: TCHP aims to shrink HER2-positive breast cancer before surgery and reduce the risk of it returning.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected. Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen. Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used. Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: All four medicines are given by infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle, for six cycles before surgery. Surgery findings guide the postoperative treatment. There is no routine take-home chemotherapy pump.
key_points: The week-12 echo is approximately before Cycle 5 only if cycles remain on time. Use elapsed time from the cardiac assessment when treatment is delayed. Breast imaging for surgical planning has an individual date; the map must not invent a universal midpoint scan.
Six cycles before surgery are one part of the pathway. Surgery findings determine the treatment afterwards; hormone treatment is added only if the cancer is also hormone-receptor positive.
Radiotherapy, endocrine therapy and HER2 continuation can overlap when the MDT considers this appropriate. The map does not prescribe exact postoperative start dates.
The echo interval runs from the HER2 treatment course; changing phase does not reset monitoring.

drug_profiles.name: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
drug_profiles.drug_class: HER2-directed antibody linked to the microtubule inhibitor DM1
drug_profiles.mechanism: HER2 binding delivers the linked DM1 payload into cells. DM1 acts on tubulin and disrupts cell division. This is one linked medicine with its own dose and toxicity rules; it is not interchangeable with trastuzumab alone or trastuzumab deruxtecan.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

drug_profiles.name: Tucatinib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits HER2 kinase activity and downstream growth signalling. In this breast regimen it is combined with capecitabine and trastuzumab, with a continuous tablet schedule separate from the capecitabine break.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

drug_profiles.name: Ribociclib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Blocks cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, slowing cell-cycle progression. Used with endocrine treatment in selected HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. Adjuvant and advanced-disease starting doses differ; use the indication-specific NCCP regimen.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

drug_profiles.name: Abemaciclib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Blocks cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, slowing cell-cycle progression. Its continuous dosing and monitoring plan differ from ribociclib. Use the specific breast indication and endocrine partner described in the NCCP regimen.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending
